content: 1. Brandt A, Samuelsson K, Toytari O, Salminen AL conducted a systematic review on the outcomes of environmental control systems and smart home technology for individuals with disabilities. The review focused on activity and participation, quality of life, and user satisfaction. (Disability & Rehabilitation Assistive Technology, 2011; 6(3): 189-206). 2. Liu CJ, Horton VE, Mears KE performed a systematic review of occupational therapy interventions aimed at improving daily activity performance at home for older adults with low vision. (American Journal of Occupational Therapy, 2013; 67(3): 279-287). 3. Chase CA, Mann K, Wasek S, Arbesman M reviewed the effects of home modification and fall prevention programs on reducing falls and improving performance among community-dwelling older adults. (American Journal of Occupational Therapy, 2012; 66(3): 284-291). 4. Clemson L, Mackenzie L, Ballinger C, Close JC, Cumming RG conducted a meta-analysis of randomized trials to evaluate environmental interventions for fall prevention in community-dwelling older adults. (Journal of Aging and Health, 2008; 20(8): 954-971). 5. Gillespie LD, Robertson MC, Gillespie WJ, Sherrington C, Gates S, Clemson LM, et al. reviewed interventions for preventing falls in older adults living in the community. (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2012; 9: CD007146). 6. Wahl AF, Oswald F, Iwarsson S examined the empirical evidence on the relationship between the home environment and disability-related outcomes in aging individuals. (Gerontologist, 2009; 49(3): 355-367). 7. The Medical Advisory Secretariat analyzed evidence-based strategies for preventing falls and fall-related injuries in community-dwelling seniors. (Ontario Health Technology Assessment Series, 2008; 8(2): 1-78). 8. Lee HC, Chang KC, Tsauo JY, Hung JW, Huang YC, Lin SI studied the effects of a multifactorial fall prevention program on fall incidence and physical function in community-dwelling older adults at risk of falls. (e1). 9. Letts L, Moreland J, Richardson J, Coman L, Edwards M, Ginis KM, et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of cross-sectional and cohort studies to assess the physical environment as a fall risk factor in older adults. (Australian Occupational Therapy Journal, 2010; 57(1): 51-64). 10. Lyons RA, John A, Brophy S, Jones SJ, Johansen A, Kemp A, et al. reviewed the modification of the home environment to reduce injuries. (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2006; 4: CD003600). 11. Nyman SR, Victor CR explored older adults' participation and engagement with fall prevention interventions in community settings, augmenting the Cochrane systematic review. (Age and Ageing, 2012; 41(1): 16-23). 12. Rubenstein LZ, Josephson KR reviewed interventions aimed at reducing multifactorial risks for falling. (Revista Española de Geriatría y Gerontología, 2005; 40(SUPPL. 2): 45-53). 13. Turner GA, Lyons RA, Mann MK, John A, Lannon S examined home environment modifications for injury reduction. (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2011; 2). 14. Schoessow K proposed a model for occupational therapy in low vision, shifting from compensation to participation. (British Journal of Occupational Therapy, 2010; 73(4): 160-169). 15. Skelton DA, Howe TE, Ballinger C, Neil F, Palmer S, Gray L reviewed environmental and behavioral interventions for reducing physical activity limitations in visually impaired older adults. (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 2013; 6: CD009233). 16. Tse T discussed the role of environmental modifications in fall prevention and their effectiveness. (Australian Occupational Therapy Journal, 2005; 52(4): 271-281). 17. Bishop M, Roessler RT, Rumrill PD, Sheppard-Jones K, Frain M, Waletich B, et al. studied the relationship between housing accessibility variables and employment status among adults with multiple sclerosis. (Journal of Rehabilitation, 2013; 79(4): 4-14). 18. Blaschke CM, Freddolino PP, Mullen EE reviewed aging and technology, focusing on assistive technologies and their impact on older adults. (British Journal of Social Work, 2009; 39(4): 641-656). 19. Bonnefoy X provided an overview of inadequate housing and its health effects. (International Journal of Environment and Pollution, 2007; 30(3-4): 411-429). 20. Bozzolini G, Cassibba S presented a case report on home accessibility improvements for a person with a disability following a spinal cord injury. (European Journal of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine, 2008; 44(4): 455-459). 21. Brooks IM shared design insights for creating wheelchair-accessible kitchens. (Abilities, 2004; 61: 30-31). 22. Gitlin LN, Winter L, Dennis MP, Hodgson N, Hauck WW conducted a randomized trial of a bio-behavioral home-based intervention for adults with dementia, including home safety training and stress reduction. (Journal of the American Medical Association, 2010; 304(9): 983-991). 23. Granbom M, Slaug B, Löfqvist C, et al. studied community relocation in very old age and its impact on housing accessibility. (American Journal of Occupational Therapy, 2016; 70: 7002270020). 24. Hanson J, Percival J examined the housing and support needs of visually impaired adults in England. (British Journal of Visual Impairment, 2005; 23(3): 102-107). 25. Riikonen M, Mäkelä K, Perälä S reviewed safety and monitoring technologies for the homes of people with dementia. (Gerontechnology, 2010; 9(1): 32-45). This list provides a detailed summary of various studies and reviews related to housing accessibility, assistive technologies, and interventions for individuals with disabilities or older adults.
